text:
maria-finance: Heads up — customer NovaHealth flagged a surprise line on their latest invoice: a 48hr surge charge on their reserved pool during a regional failover. They say they only had traffic consistent with normal usage. Can we audit?
aj-sales: FYI they hit the automatic failover last Friday around 02:15 UTC when us-west went read-only. Might explain burst events.
maria-finance: I get that, but this is showing as a separate 'surge' metering charge instead of failover consumption against their reserved commit. We need to confirm whether it should have applied to reserved capacity vs overage.
sam-accounting: Pulling invoice INV-8429 now. Line item is: "Reserved Surge - us-west-2 - 2026-03-19 00:00 to 2026-03-21 23:59" for ~720k token units.
elaine-cs: Customer sent logs showing request ids and timestamps, they already raised a support case. They asked for a provisional credit while we investigate.
maria-finance: What does product/ops say on routing? Was traffic routed to a non-reserved pool or a different nodepool without commit attribution?

tony-ops: Checking routing history — during the failover we routed traffic to the cross-region fallback pool. That pool is attached to a different reserved commit (acct: commit-9) shared across several customers. NovaHealth's commit is commit-3. There was a short window (~1h40m) where the cluster autoscaler spun up new nodes tagged with the fallback pool and usage was metered under untagged nodepools.

sam-accounting: If usage was metered under untagged or wrong pool, meter key will show as 'unallocated'. I can query the billing exports for those hours. Give me the exact minute window you saw.
ton y-ops: typo — tony-ops: the heavy spike is 02:14:30 to 03:52:10 UTC. I'll paste the nodepool ids: np-fallback-03, np-fallback-04.

sam-accounting: Running query now against metering dataset. If match, we can reattribute usage to commit-3 retroactively if policy allows. That would remove the surge charge and apply against their reserved units.
maria-finance: Policy note: we allow reclassification for failover events if the routing was automatic and customer didn't change config, but we still need sign-off from product and operations. Also need to confirm commit utilization caps.

aj-sales: Customer expectation: no surprise overages for platform-initiated failovers. They want a credit and a config or contract note to avoid future similar charges.

tony-ops: I can provide an ops blameless incident note and confirm the routing decision. We put fallback pools in place to protect latency; not intended to trigger overage charges on customers.

sam-accounting: Query results: there are ~712,340 token units billed to meter_key: unallocated between those timestamps. 93% of those requests carry NovaHealth's org id in the request metadata. Looks like meter attribution failed.

billing-bot: Automated alert: metering anomaly detected for org=novahealth during 2319991280-2319994830. Created ticket BILL-5932.
maria-finance: OK. Proposed path: 1) provisional credit equal to the surge line item while we complete reclassification, 2) if reclassification succeeds, apply usage to reserved commit and void provisional credit, 3) if not, negotiate partial credit. Approve?

aj-sales: Approve provisional credit to keep customer calm. We should be explicit in communication: this is provisional pending reclassification.
elain e-cs: typo — elaine-cs: I'll notify NovaHealth support case with provisional credit note and expected timeline (48 hours).

sam-accounting: Next steps for me: submit a reclassification request to billing pipeline and attach meter evidence (org tags, request ids). I'll mark the request as high priority referencing BILL-5932.

tony-ops: I'll add the incident note and confirm the failover was product-controlled. Also will add engineering task to ensure fallback pools inherit commit tags or we add automatic tag propagation on failover.
maria-finance: Good. For audit trail please capture: invoice line id, meter rows, request ids, nodepool ids, and the decision thread. We'll need the approval to be recorded in finance.

aj-sales: Recording approval: "Provisional credit approved by AJ (sales) and Maria (finance)."
maria-finance: I'll prepare the provisional credit memos and route to accounting to issue credit memo CM-1124. Sam, can you mark accounting hold and set a 7-day expiry on the provisional credit if reclassification unresolved?
sam-accounting: Will do. Creating hold and tagging CM-1124 as provisional.

elaine-cs: Sent customer update: "We've issued a provisional credit while we investigate routing attribution. Target resolution 48 hours." Customer replied with :+1:.
maria-finance: Thanks. One more ask: Tony, can you drop the small query snippet you used so accounting can reproduce?
tony-ops: Paste below:
```
SELECT meter_time, meter_key, org_id, nodepool_id, token_units
FROM billing_raw
WHERE meter_time BETWEEN '2026-03-19T02:14:00Z' AND '2026-03-19T03:53:00Z'
AND org_id = 'novahealth'
ORDER BY meter_time;
```

sam-accounting: Got it. I'll run and attach results to BILL-5932.
maria-finance: Thanks team. If reclassification completes we will reverse CM-1124 and apply usage to commit-3. If not, we'll propose a goodwill credit equal to 50-75% depending on circumstances. Keep me posted.

aj-sales: I'll follow up with the customer after engineering confirms mitigation plan.

billing-bot: Update: BILL-5932 status changed to in_progress by sam-accounting at 2319991450.

sam-accounting: Status update 2319991850 — reclassification successful. 705,980 token units reattributed to commit-3. Provisional credit CM-1124 to be voided and invoice updated. Attaching reconciliation CSV to BILL-5932.
maria-finance: Excellent. Closing loop with customer and finance records. Great job.
